headline: Santa Ana winds with an unusually strong north push bring highs in the 80s to Glendale and other LA and Ventura County valley and coastal areas on Thanksgiving and Friday, with wind advisories likely, before a weekend cooldown and a potentially strong rainstorm late next Tuesday into Wednesday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: The rest of Tuesday night and Wednesday stay dry around Glendale and across Los Angeles County as offshore winds (blowing from inland toward the coast) start to build; Burbank and LAX stay clear, with no wind issues at Burbank and any east wind at LAX staying under about 8 mph. Low clouds and a warmer air mass keep tonight milder than last night in inland areas, so no frost or freeze alerts are expected. A Northern California storm just barely skims San Luis Obispo County, giving the Central Coast a slight chance of light showers tonight into Wednesday morning (about a 30 percent chance of showers or low clouds around Santa Maria, San Luis Obispo and Paso Robles from 2 AM to 7 AM, plus a 30 percent chance of very low clouds or fog from 2 AM to 10 AM), with any rain likely under a tenth of an inch.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Offshore winds peak around Thanksgiving morning with a strong push from the north as well as the northeast, which tends to send stronger northerly winds into the LA valleys, including the Glendale and Burbank areas, and less wind across western Ventura County than a typical Santa Ana. Along with high pressure building over California, this pushes highs into the 80s on Thanksgiving and Friday in many coastal and valley areas of LA and Ventura Counties and well into the 70s on the Central Coast. At least low-end wind advisories are a good bet on both Thursday and Friday across parts of LA and Ventura Counties.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Cooling begins over the weekend, and Sunday is dry but cooler as high pressure shifts east ahead of a storm heading into the Pacific Northwest. The tail end of that storm will likely bring light rain to Southern California Sunday night into Monday, mostly under half an inch. A second, much stronger storm is likely right behind it late next Tuesday into Wednesday, with computer models consistently showing at least a moderate and possibly strong storm: widespread rain of at least 1–2 inches and 2–5 inches on mountain slopes facing the storm over a 6–8 hour period. Neither storm is especially cold, so any snow should stay above about 8,000 feet.

coast: A large, long-period west swell peaks Wednesday and Thursday and combines with very high tides to bring large surf and moderate to significant coastal flooding, especially around high tide in low-lying, unprotected spots, with coastal structures at increased risk of damage. The worst is expected on the Central Coast from Point Conception north, the Ventura County coast and the far eastern Santa Barbara south coast, with somewhat smaller but still concerning problems elsewhere: strong rip currents nearly everywhere, strong along-shore currents, sneaker waves, heavy shore break, beach erosion and an increased drowning risk. Central Coast beaches have a Coastal Flood Warning and High Surf Warning from 6 AM Wednesday to noon Thursday, and Ventura County beaches have the same warnings from 8 AM Wednesday to noon Thursday (advisories until then). Malibu and Los Angeles County beaches have a Coastal Flood Advisory until 6 AM Thursday, a Coastal Flood Watch Thursday morning, and a High Surf Advisory from 10 AM Wednesday to 9 PM Thursday (the advisory also covers Catalina and the Santa Barbara islands); the Santa Barbara south coast has a Coastal Flood Advisory until noon Thursday and a High Surf Advisory from 8 AM Wednesday to noon Thursday. For boaters, Small Craft Advisories run through 3 PM Thursday (some waters starting Wednesday or early Thursday), with seas peaking Wednesday at 14–19 feet on the outer waters and 13–17 feet north of Point Sal, and large breaking waves near harbor entrances that can capsize small boats. Closer in, advisory-level winds are expected in the western Santa Barbara Channel Wednesday and from Point Mugu to Santa Monica Thursday, with a 40–60 percent chance of widespread advisory-level seas Wednesday through Thursday. Friday night through Sunday brings lighter winds, though rough seas may linger offshore (50–70 percent chance) and north of Point Sal (40–60 percent), and the western Santa Barbara Channel has a 50 percent chance of advisory-level winds Sunday afternoon and evening.
watch_for: Likely wind advisories Thanksgiving and Friday in parts of LA and Ventura Counties, with stronger-than-usual north winds into the LA valleys around Glendale.
Coastal flood and high surf warnings Wednesday into Thursday on the Central Coast and Ventura County beaches, and a Coastal Flood Watch for LA County beaches Thursday morning.
A potentially strong storm late next Tuesday into Wednesday with 1–2 inches of rain widely and 2–5 inches on mountain slopes.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the dry, warm, windy stretch through Friday, and models have been consistent for several runs on next week's stronger storm, though whether it ends up moderate or strong is still uncertain.
